session_covered: US session of Monday 16 November (European session also lower)
intro: Covers the Monday 16 November US session (European session also lower). Published after an 08:15 retry to settle conflicting SPI futures readings; the SPI figure is a range and some figures are approximate (see notes).
footnotes: US index figures are from FNArena's post-close snapshot, consistent with ABC and Reuters (Dow). Other reports gave S&P 500 7,400-7,427 (-1.8% to -2.1%), Nasdaq 24,469-24,557 (-2.3% to -2.65%) and Dow 51,516-51,689 (-1.3% to -1.6%).
10-year yield per FNArena; Trading Economics and Reuters showed 5.13%, down 1-2bp. AUD/USD per FNArena; one source showed 0.6739 with a different base.
Brent per Bloomberg via Motley Fool (Trading Economics 92.17, -3.84%). Gold is a CFD-based spot price (other sources 3,853-3,863). Iron ore is the prior-session print (another source 91.48, -0.13%).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures point lower: down roughly 0.5-0.8% (December contract about 9,032-9,041; ABC -0.5% to 9,041, Motley Fool -0.75% / -68 points, Investing.com 9,032, -0.79%). Using the midpoint of -0.65%, the implied ASX 200 open is about 8,986, roughly 59 points lower. The ASX 200 closed Monday at 9,044.7, down 0.41%.

local_events: RBA Governor Michele Bullock speaks at the ASIC Annual Forum at 10:00 AEDT
RBA board meeting minutes at 11:30 AEDT
what_moved: AI and chip stocks led a broad sell-off ahead of Nvidia's earnings (due Tuesday US time) and Anthropic's IPO, after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation and a new US rule restricting China's access to advanced AI chips. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 4.6% and Nvidia about 4-5%; decliners outnumbered advancers about 3.2-to-1. An S&P 500 sector breakdown was not available in the sources retrieved.

news.headline: Nvidia CEO resigns before earnings.
news.summary: Jensen Huang resigned last week; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia has lost about US$1.9 trillion of market value since early October.

news.headline: US tightens China AI-chip access.
news.summary: A new interim rule restricts China's access to top AI chips, issued ahead of a planned Trump-Xi meeting. The Nasdaq is now more than 10% below its 6 October record close.

news.headline: Fed hike pricing.
news.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said AI could either lift growth or raise unemployment; CME FedWatch priced a 93.7% chance of a 25bp December hike, while Reuters cited about an 8% chance of a half-point move.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO nears.
news.summary: The offer is set to price Wednesday US time, with Nasdaq trading a day later, and is reportedly about seven times oversubscribed.

news.headline: Asia sold off.
news.summary: Taiex fell more than 4% and Japan and South Korea slumped on AI caution; Democrats' US midterm win raised concern about tougher data-centre regulation.

news.headline: Oil and gold slide.
news.summary: Brent fell about 3.7% to near US$92/bbl, and a stronger US dollar pushed gold to a one-year low.

news.headline: ASX ended lower Monday.
news.summary: The ASX 200 fell 0.41% to 9,044.7, led down by miners (materials -2.17%).

coming_up: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings after the US close on Tuesday 17 November (US time); US retail sales are also due Tuesday. Fed October meeting minutes are due Wednesday 18 November (US time), and Anthropic's IPO is due to price the same day.
